image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a male mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The duck is facing left but looking back over its shoulder towards the right. It features a glossy iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a yellow-green bill, and a body with mottled brown and grey plumage. The tail shows characteristic curled black central feathers and white side feathers. The background is blurred water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a yellow-green coloration consistent with a mallard drake.
The visible eye is dark and round, matching the biological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears robust and floats naturally on the water surface. The plumage texture looks dense and layered.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, white neck ring, and brownish-grey body plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged or occluded by the body and water; they are not visible in this frame.
The folded wings are visible along the side of the body, appearing broad and structurally sound, though the 'pointed' nature is less obvious when folded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, showing the characteristic upward curl of the central black feathers and white lateral feathers.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The feather texture on the lower left flank appears slightly smudged or painterly compared to the sharp detail on the head. Some feather boundaries blend into each other rather than having distinct edges, suggesting minor generative smoothing.
The transition from the white neck ring to the body plumage is slightly soft and lacks the crisp definition seen in high-resolution photography, though it remains biologically plausible.

Check if the white neck ring is a clean, continuous band or if it bleeds into the green head or brown body. Verify that the reflection in the water matches the shape of the duck's underside.
